entry.title: Fix IntegrityViolationReport and Integrity-Policy examples and prose
entry.content:
Description

Integrity Violation documentation has inaccurately, most likely due to being outdated.

Motivation

Fixing this is important for accuracy. My motivation is I noticed issues when comparing to observed behaviour and specifications.

Additional details

  • Update destination on IntegrityViolationReport to allow "script" or "style" per W3C SRI (#destination).
  • Fix Structured Fields syntax in IntegrityViolationReport's Reporting-Endpoints (quoted strings) and Integrity-Policy (space-separated inner list) examples per RFC 9651.
  • Fix server report payload examples on both pages to use a JSON array (application/reports+json) with numeric age and user_agent per W3C Reporting API (#serialize-reports).
  • Fix crossorigin attribute spelling and IntegrityViolationReportBody reference.

Specifications:

  • https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#destination
  • https://w3c.github.io/reporting/#serialize-reports
  • https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9651#section-3.1.1
  • https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9651#section-3.3.3

Captured browser report examples:

entry.title: Add the message_serialization manifest key page
entry.content:
Description

Adds a page for the message_serialization manifest key and updates the Chrome bullet in "Data cloning algorithm" on the Chrome incompatibilities page.

Motivation

Chrome 148 supports the key and Safari Technology Preview 257 adds it. With "structured_clone", an extension sends messages with the structured clone algorithm instead of JSON. The page covers the values, the default, the differences from JSON serialization (toJSON(), function values, Proxy, class instances), an example that keeps toJSON() while opted in, and how Chrome and Safari handle mismatched formats and messages from web pages. The Chrome bullet previously said Chrome may switch to structured cloning in the future.

Additional details

  • w3c/webextensions#931
  • https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/whats-new
  • https://webkit.org/b/330104

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46590

Depends on: mdn/browser-compat-data#31193, which adds the webextensions.manifest.message_serialization compatibility data the page's {{Compat}} macro reads.

entry.title: SVG begin: note that accessKey() is unsupported and fix the keyboard example
entry.content:
Description

The begin attribute page described <accessKey-value> as a working value and had a live "Accesskey example" that does nothing in any browser. This PR:

  • adds a note under <accessKey-value> that no browser supports it, and how to start an animation from the keyboard instead;
  • replaces the broken example with a working "Keyboard example": the <animate> element gets id="grow" and begin="indefinite", and a keydown listener calls beginElement() when s is pressed. This is the alternative suggested in the issue. The rest of the example (rectangle, label, grid) is unchanged.

Motivation

Readers who copy the example or try the live sample get an animation that never starts, with no explanation.

Additional details

As researched in the issue:

  • Firefox removed accessKey() in Firefox 59 (bug 1423098).
  • WebKit and Chromium parse accesskey( but never connect it to keyboard input (// FIXME: accesskey() support. in both). They also match only the lowercase spelling, so accessKey(s) is treated as an event name that never fires.

I left the spec-urls front matter (svgwg.org) unchanged. Sibling pages such as end use the same host, and the front-matter linter validates spec URLs, so changing that host is probably better as a separate, site-wide change.

Checked locally: prettier@3.10.1 -c and markdownlint-cli2@0.24.1 with the repository's config both pass.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46580

entry.title: Remove version references from the Extend the developer tools article
entry.content:
Description

Updates the "Extend the developer tools" article and the devtools API reference to describe Firefox and Safari support without referencing specific Firefox versions (which addresses an earlier comment about removing devtools references to Firefox 54 and 55. Also removes reference pages for devtools.inspectedWindow features that neither Firefox nor Safari supports.

Changes:

  • Extend the developer tools:
    • Rewrote the opening note to remove "Firefox 55" and to say that Firefox and Safari don't implement all the Chrome devtools API features.
    • Renamed "Limitations of the devtools APIs" to "Cross-browser support for devtools APIs". It now lists features not supported in both Firefox and Safari, in Firefox only, and in Safari only. It no longer mentions Firefox 54, and it no longer says support for most features is coming.
    • Removed panels.elements and panels.ElementsPanel from the Firefox unsupported features, as Firefox has supported them since version 56.
    • Added ExtensionPanel.onSearch, ExtensionSidebarPane.setHeight(), the inspectedWindow.Resource type, and the inspectedWindow.eval() options to the unsupported features.
    • Removed "starting from Firefox 55" from the note on $0 and inspect().
  • devtools.inspectedWindow: rewrote the note to remove "Firefox 54" and cover Safari. It also states that the reference documents only the features that Firefox or Safari support.
  • devtools.panels: updated the note to cover Safari.
  • Removed the inspectedWindow.Resource, inspectedWindow.getResources(), inspectedWindow.onResourceAdded, and inspectedWindow.onResourceContentCommitted pages and their entries on the devtools.inspectedWindow page. These features are Chrome-only; BCD previously listed them as supported in Safari 16 (see Related issues and pull requests). Each page redirects to the "Cross-browser support for devtools APIs" section.
  • Updated links to the renamed section.

Related issues and pull requests

Related BCD changes in mdn/browser-compat-data#31186, which corrects Safari support for the devtools.inspectedWindow and devtools.panels features, and mdn/browser-compat-data#31154, which corrects the eval() options.

Replaces #28132, which proposed removing browser-specific references from this article.

entry.title: build(deps-dev): bump cspell from 10.5.0 to 10.5.1 in the npm-dev group
entry.content:
Bumps the npm-dev group with 1 update: cspell.

Updates cspell from 10.5.0 to 10.5.1

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.5.1

Fixes

fix: Let --force-check check files skipped by ignorePathPresets (#9634)

With --force-check, cspell lint now checks git's own files when they are named on the command line. Before, they were still skipped by the git preset of ignorePathPresets, even though --force-check already overrides ignorePaths and --exclude.

cspell lint --force-check --file .git/config

Before:

CSpell: Files checked: 0, skipped: 1, Issues found: 0 in 0 files.
No files found to check (1 skipped).

After:

.git/config:1:1 - Unknown word (zqxword)
CSpell: Files checked: 1, Issues found: 1 in 1 file.

This also covers the .git file that git puts in a worktree or a submodule.

fix: Spell check .env files like .env.* files (#9624)

Summary

.env and .env.* files, such as .env.local, are now spell checked the same way. Before, .env was treated as a properties file, while .env.* files were treated as shell scripts. A word could pass in .env.local and be flagged in .env.

Both now have both file types, properties and shellscript. So .env files now also use the shell, Bash, and Git dictionaries, and any languageSettings for either file type apply to both. .envrc is still a shell script only.

entry.title: CSS: use {{CSSInfo}} for color-interpolation
entry.content:
Description

Replaces the hand-written formal-definition table on the color-interpolation page with {{CSSInfo}}, now that mdn-data has the property (mdn/data#1121, released in mdn-data 2.38.0).

Motivation

The hand-written table was wrong in two places:

  • Default value: it said auto. The SVG 2 definition gives sRGB, and so do Chromium (css_properties.json5), Gecko (longhands.toml) and WebKit (CSSProperties.json). WPT's svg/painting/inheritance.svg tests it. The page's own sRGB entry already says it's the default.
  • Applies to: it listed only <linearGradient> and <radialGradient>. The spec says container elements, graphics elements, gradient elements, <use> and <animate>.

{{CSSInfo}} also adds the rows the table didn't have, such as inherited, percentages and computed value.

Additional details

Built the page locally with rari 1.3.0, which pulled mdn-data 2.38.0. The rendered table shows initial value sRGB, applies to "Container elements, graphics elements, gradient elements, <use>, and <animate> in <svg>", inherited yes, computed value as specified, and animation type discrete.

Related issues and pull requests

  • mdn/data#1121 adds color-interpolation to mdn-data.

entry.title: [Technical review] Add WebDriver Classic Navigate To and Get Current URL pages
entry.content:
Description

Added pages for the following commands of the Navigation chapter of WebDriver Classic:

  • Get Current URL
  • Navigate To

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#navigate-to
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#get-current-url

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Chrome

  • Navigate To and invalid certificates. With acceptInsecureCerts set to false, navigating to a page with a self-signed certificate returned null and loaded the "Privacy error" interstitial, where the spec returns insecure certificate (seen in my test run, headless and headed). BCD shows Navigate To as supported since Chrome 65 with no note about this.
  • Outdated w3c note. BCD's Chrome entries for both commands say to include {"goog:chromeOptions": {"w3c": true}} in the capabilities. My test sessions didn't set it, and both commands returned W3C responses.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the BCD update.
